site.name: Crackspread
site.description: Is there enough oil? World supply and demand, refinery margins, and what they do to diesel, food and flights. Public data, updated three times a day.
common.unavailable: Not available right now. The last update did not return this data.
common.stale_title: Not refreshed since {date}. Showing the last known value.
common.proposal: News reports mention {value} ({source}, {date}). Not yet in the ledger.
common.lang.label: Language
hero.title: Is there enough oil?
hero.lede.deficit: Not quite. The world pumps {p} million barrels a day and uses {c}. The missing {g} million a day comes out of storage.
hero.lede.surplus: Yes, for now. The world pumps {p} million barrels a day and uses {c}. The extra {g} million a day goes into storage.
hero.lede.balanced: Just about. The world pumps {p} million barrels a day and uses {c}. Storage barely moves.
hero.lede_nodata: Supply and demand figures are not available right now.
hero.chart_label: Supply and demand by month, mb/d
crack.title: Crack spreads
crack.lede: A crack spread is a refinery's margin: what a product sells for minus what the crude cost. Diesel is the one to watch.
crack.scale_label: Diesel crack, percentile of all trading days since {start}
crack.percentile: The diesel crack is higher than {pct}% of all trading days since {start}.
crack.table.note: Last {n} points of the chart. The full series is in prices.json.
crack.spread_fact: Brent is trading ${v} above WTI. The 2015–19 average gap was ${mean}.
crack.footnote: NY Harbor ULSD minus Brent. Other benchmarks (Europe, Singapore) can read higher.

wb.world: Starting point: about {p} mb/d pumped, about {c} used. {note}
wb.world_plain: Starting point: about {p} mb/d pumped, about {c} used.

countries.title: Who pumps, who uses

ship.cost.title: Shipping cost per barrel

ship.label: Per Max Fisher and news reports, not live data
groc.title: Diesel, and what it carries
groc.lede: Diesel moves trucks, tractors, ships and generators, so a diesel squeeze shows up in food, freight and flights.
groc.products: What a barrel of oil becomes
groc.label: Whiteboard figures: Max Fisher's estimate, not live data
news.title: Today
news.lede: What changed in the oil market, from the last two days of headlines. Every line links to its source.
news.fallback: No AI summary this run. This is a rule-based digest of the data and headlines.
news.empty: No headlines for this topic right now.
news.feeds_failed: Feeds that did not answer this run: {list}
meth.title: Method
meth.formula.diesel: Diesel crack = NY Harbor ULSD ($/gal) × 42 − Brent ($/bbl)
meth.formula.gasoline: Gasoline crack = NY Harbor gasoline ($/gal) × 42 − Brent ($/bbl)
meth.formula.jet: Jet crack = US Gulf jet fuel ($/gal) × 42 − Brent ($/bbl)
meth.series: FRED series: {ids}. A crack is computed only for days on which every input exists; holidays are skipped.
meth.benchmark: Max Fisher's whiteboard mentions a record diesel crack of about ${fisher}/bbl. The US benchmark used here (NY Harbor ULSD minus Brent) reads ${ours}/bbl and peaked at ${max}/bbl on {max_date}. He probably refers to a different benchmark, such as European gasoil or Singapore, so his figure appears only in the whiteboard section, labelled as his estimate.
meth.steo: The balance comes from the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook. The current month is an estimate, later months are forecasts, and both are revised every month.
meth.updates: The site updates three times a day at about {times} ({tz}). Scheduled runs can be up to half an hour late.
meth.stale: If a source does not answer, the last known value stays and is marked stale with its date. Gaps are never filled with estimates. Prices count as stale after {prices} hours, the outlook after {steo} hours, news after {news} hours.
meth.history: The chart shows weekly values before {date} and daily values after. The percentile uses the full daily history since {start}.
meth.sources_note: Every number on this page carries its source and date next to it.
donate.title: Fuel the humans
donate.0.headline: Buy me a cup of liquid gold that fuels humans.
donate.0.sub: Coffee: the only crude worth refining. Crackspread is free, ad-free and tracker-free. If it saved you an hour of doom-scrolling, top up the tank.
donate.1.headline: This site runs on two fuels: public data and coffee. Only one of them is free.
donate.2.headline: Help keep the crack spread wide and the coffee spread wider.
donate.3.headline: No ads, no paywall, no barrels. Just a tip jar with excellent margins.
donate.fineprint: Donations go to a person, not a hedge fund. They don't change what the data says.
footer.src.fred: Source: FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; data: U.S. EIA. Public domain.
footer.src.eia: U.S. Energy Information Administration: Short-Term Energy Outlook and International Energy Data. Public domain.
footer.src.portwatch: IMF PortWatch, daily chokepoint transits (CC BY 4.0).
meth.shipping: Tanker traffic comes from IMF PortWatch, which counts ship transponder (AIS) transits per chokepoint and day. The site averages the last {days} days and compares them with the previous calendar year's daily average. PortWatch publishes with a few days' delay.
footer.src.news: Headlines: rights stay with the publishers. This site only links.
footer.src.manual: Whiteboard figures: Max Fisher's estimates, maintained by hand, labelled as such.
footer.src.fonts: Wordmark: Permanent Marker (Apache 2.0). Chart: uPlot (MIT). Code: MIT. Data belongs to its sources.
footer.disclaimer: Not financial advice. Not trading advice. Not even dinner-party advice. Numbers come from the sources listed; jokes come from us.
footer.nocookies: No ads, no tracking, no cookies.
